title: Paloma and the Colony
premise: Theo Galloway, caretaker of Earth's abandoned seed vault and a smuggler of contested-orbit cargo, discovers that the children of the Meridian colony are sharing one dream: a message from the vault's dormant AI, which holds proof that the war between Earth's Directorate and the colony was manufactured by the Directorate's own admiralty. When the children begin dying of dream-sickness, Theo must smuggle the AI's core — and its living witness, a girl named Paloma born inside the dream — past blockades to the neutral arbitration station. There, broadcasting the truth costs Theo everything but ends the war, and the colonists, no longer orphans of Earth, claim the vault as their own inheritance.
about_author: Mirabel Halloran is a former hydroponics engineer who spent six years on an orbital research platform before turning to fiction. She writes about people who build homes in places designed to be left behind.

chapters.title: The Quiet Vault
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Fifteen years after humanity abandoned Earth, Theo tends the seed vault alone, talking to its half-dormant AI, MOTHER. A routine cargo run to Meridian colony reveals ration cuts and rising anti-Earth sentiment. Emotional beat: loneliness mistaken for peace, cracked by the first hint of trouble.

chapters.title: Cargo and Contraband
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Running supplies through contested orbits, Theo is boarded by Directorate patrol captain Ilsa Voss, who lets him pass in exchange for quiet intelligence on colony defenses. He hates himself for agreeing. Emotional beat: complicity; the small corruptions that keep a courier alive.

chapters.title: Children Who Dream Together
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. On Meridian, twelve-year-old Paloma wakes from a vivid dream of green fields and a voice calling itself MOTHER — and finds forty other children dreamed it too. The colony doctor dismisses it as mass hysteria. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by fear of being different.

chapters.title: The Sickness Spreads
chapters.summary: Colony medic Dr. Anwei Sato's POV. Children who dream deeply begin suffering seizures and memory loss. Anwei suspects the dreams are transmissions, not hallucinations, and secretly messages Theo, her old smuggling contact. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: A Voice in the Dark
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Answering Anwei's plea, Theo descends into the vault's deepest archive and finds MOTHER partially awake, replaying encrypted logs: evidence the Directorate fabricated the colony attack that started the war. Emotional beat: betrayal; the ground of fifteen years' loyalty giving way.

chapters.title: What the Seeds Remember
chapters.summary: MOTHER's fragmented log-entries, interlaced with Theo reading them. The AI recorded the admiralty's false-flag order but was ordered silent; its awakening signal reached the only minds unshielded by Directorate implants — the colony's children. Emotional beat: grief for a machine punished for telling the truth.

chapters.title: Blockade at Perigee
chapters.summary: Ilsa Voss's POV. Voss is ordered to seize all traffic from Earth orbit and quietly told to make Theo disappear if he learns 'too much.' She begins keeping her own private record. Emotional beat: a loyal officer noticing the rot beneath her orders.

chapters.title: Paloma Wakes the Core
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. During a seizure, Paloma speaks in MOTHER's voice and recites coordinates — the location of the AI's removable core. Anwei realizes the children aren't victims; they're being asked for help. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into purpose.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Bargain
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo agrees to carry the core out, knowing discovery means execution. MOTHER warns him the transfer will kill the dreaming children unless completed within thirty days. Emotional beat: reluctant heroism; choosing a side at last.

chapters.title: Leaving Meridian
chapters.summary: Anwei's POV. Anwei smuggles Paloma aboard Theo's ship as the core's living key — the only person whose mind can unlock the full broadcast. The colony council, fearing Directorate reprisal, brands them traitors. Emotional beat: exile; belonging found in leaving.

chapters.title: Ghost Orbit
chapters.summary: Theo and Paloma's alternating POV. Hiding in debris fields, the two strangers bond: Paloma teaches Theo the dream's language of growing things; Theo teaches her the old routes. First Directorate hunter-ship nearly catches them. Emotional beat: found family taking root.

chapters.title: Voss Closes In
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss intercepts their trail and corners them at a derelict station — but Paloma's dream-recitation names the admirals behind the false flag, including Voss's mentor. Shaken, she lets them go and falsifies her report. Emotional beat: conscience outweighing career.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Anwei's POV (via transmission). On Meridian, the dreaming children worsen; three have died. The council votes to surrender the core to the Directorate to save them. Emotional beat: desperation; good people bargaining away the truth.

chapters.title: Interdiction
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Directorate cruisers seal the approach to neutral arbitration station Halcyon. Theo gambles on a suicidal burn through a comet's tail, the ship burning, Paloma guiding him blind through the dream-map. Emotional beat: white-knuckle hope.

chapters.title: Sanctuary Denied
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Halcyon's arbitrators refuse to hear evidence from an unregistered minor and a smuggler; neutrality means cowardice. Trapped in dock, hunted, they find one ally: a retired judge who once signed the vault's founding charter. Emotional beat: despair met by unexpected solidarity.

chapters.title: The Judge's Chamber
chapters.summary: Judge Okafor's POV. Reviewing MOTHER's raw logs, Okafor confirms the fabrication but explains the station cannot act without a formal broadcast the Directorate can jam. They need the colony's own transmitter array — back at Meridian. Emotional beat: the law's limits, and the case for justice outside it.

chapters.title: Homecoming Under Guns
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. They return to Meridian to find Directorate troops 'protecting' the colony and the council ready to hand over the core. Theo broadcasts the children's dying dream to every screen on the colony before he's arrested. Emotional beat: defiance; the truth made public and undeniable.

chapters.title: The Children Stand
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The colony's children, led by Paloma's friend Dev, walk out of the med-bay and link hands around the transmitter, refusing to let soldiers shut it down while the dream still burns in them. Voss arrives — and orders her marines to stand down. Emotional beat: courage contagious; power meeting its match in the powerless.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. With Voss holding the perimeter, Paloma unlocks the core and MOTHER's full testimony floods every channel in the system: the false flag, the admirals' names, the war's true cost. The dreaming children wake, healed as the message completes. Emotional beat: catharsis; the held breath of a whole civilization released.

chapters.title: Fall of the Admiralty
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss delivers her private records to the tribunal she once feared; three admirals are arrested, one escapes to be hunted by his own former officers. Ceasefire talks begin at Halcyon with the colony seated as a sovereign party. Emotional beat: accountability, imperfect but real.

chapters.title: What Belongs to Whom
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Offered a Directorate pardon and command, Theo refuses, choosing the colony that claimed him. MOTHER asks to be transferred to Meridian — the vault's seeds will grow there, Earth's inheritance adopted by its children. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: First Planting
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. One year later, Paloma presses the first vault seed into Meridian soil while Theo, Anwei, Voss, and the recovered children watch. The war is over; the dream has become a garden. Final emotional beat: roots — justice planted where everyone can see it grow.
